newsitem.title: USA: Yahoo!, NBC in Internet chat deal.
newsitem.headline: Yahoo!, NBC in Internet chat deal.

text.p: Yahoo! Inc. and General Electric Corp.'s NBC television network said Monday Yahoo! Chat users will soon be able to talk to stars from NBC television programmes in regular online chat sessions.

Under terms of the agreement, Yahoo! Chat users will be able to tune in to NBC Live, a new dedicated NBC chat area on its service. Last week Yahoo! said its chat services had passed the 1 million-user milestone.

The companies said each week NBC Live will feature two chats with stars from NBC's prime-time series, soap operas, movies and miniseries, beginning with a party next Saturday from NBC's semi-annual press tour in Pasedena, Calif.
Advertising on the NBC Live area will be sold by Yahoo!, with assistance from NBC Interactive, the companies said.
NBC will publicise NBC Live events on air during prime-time viewing hours and Yahoo! will promote the service on its main Web site, http://www.yahoo.com.

Yahoo! stock jumped to a record trading high, closing at the day's peak, up $4.50 at $48.50 on Nasdaq. Stock in General Electric Co., which owns NBC, ended up 37.5 cents at $71 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts attributed the rise in Yahoo! to various factors, including continued zeal over Internet deals, rather than to any specific news.
"This is a frothy stock market. This is just classic stock market behaviour," said Keith Benjamin, an analyst at the San Francisco firm of Robertson Stephens & Co.
